prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A quick-reference prayer-time table for Saudi cities: one city per row, with five daily prayer times to compare across cities and across prayers.","reading":"Right-to-left: the reader finds the city in the rightmost column, then scans leftward across the five prayer-time columns; vertical scanning compares the same prayer across cities, so the five time columns need a consistent rhythm.","groups":["Column 1 is the row identifier and should be visually separate from the data.","Columns 2–6 form one parallel group of prayer times; they share the same value type and should read as a coherent block, with الفجر/الظهر/العصر as the daytime run and المغرب/العشاء as the evening pair."],"keep_intact":["HH:MM time values must never split across lines.","City names should ideally stay on one line; if not, they must wrap only at spaces between words.","Arabic header words should not be broken mid-word if avoidable."],"may_wrap":["Long city names such as المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة at word spaces.","Longer prayer headers such as المغرب and العشاء if the column budget is tight; row height can absorb a second header line."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [112, 49, 49, 49, 51, 49] · table 360×418px · row heights [60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 5/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 11
Design r0B: widths [70, 56, 56, 59, 62, 56] · table 360×325px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 2/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [112, 56, 56, 59, 68, 62] · table 414×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 54px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"The city column is generous enough that every city name sits on one line, including المدينة المنورة, so the identifier column reads as a clean, confident stack; the city block is also clearly separated from the data block.","problems":"The prayer block is destroyed: 5 of 6 headers wrap (العشاء becomes 'الع' / 'شاء') and there are 11 mid-word splits, including inside the clock values themselves ('8:1' / '6', '3:3' / '8'). A prayer time broken across two lines is no longer a time — the reader cannot compare vertically at all. Rows balloon to 60px and the table grows to 418px tall, so a 7-row quick reference becomes a long scroll.","cause":"112px on a column that only needs 91 leaves 49–51px for the five time columns, i.e. 28–30px of usable text against the 35–47px their headers and values require. Over-allocation to col 1 is the single cause of everything else."},{"design":"r0B","good":"It fits the 360px box, every time value stays whole on one line, and no data cell splits mid-word. The rows read as units and the whole table is compact at 325px — this is by far the best starting point.","problems":"Two single-word headers break mid-word, leaving ugly orphans: المغرب renders as 'المغر' / 'ب' and العشاء as 'العشا' / 'ء'. A one-letter fragment under a header looks like a rendering bug. Row heights are also uneven (60/36 alternating), which breaks the vertical rhythm of the comparison.","cause":"70px on the city column is exactly the minimum that keeps 'المدينة' (49px unbreakable) intact, so it cannot give more; that leaves 289px for five columns that need 301px. المغرب at 62 (41px text vs 47 needed) and العشاء at 56 (35 vs 41 needed) are each 6–12px short, and a shortfall on a single-word Arabic header always manifests as a mid-word break. The two wrapped cities are simply what 70px costs."},{"design":"r0C","good":"Perfect typographic rhythm: all headers, all times and all city names on one line, uniform 36px rows, 255px total, and the five prayer columns read as one coherent parallel block with the city clearly separate. As pure typesetting it is the best of the three.","problems":"At 414px it overflows the 360px box by 54px, so the reader must scroll horizontally and can never see the city name and the leftmost prayer time in the same view — which defeats the purpose of a table whose whole job is cross-prayer and cross-city comparison.","cause":"It spends 112px on the city column (21px more than needed for one-line cities) on top of the five full-need prayer columns (56/56/59/68/62 = 301), summing to 413. The city column is the only place where fat can be trimmed."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"intact-371","widths":[70,56,56,59,68,62],"change":"Take r0C's exact per-column needs — 56/56/59/68/62 is precisely what keeps الفجر, الظهر, العصر, المغرب and العشاء whole — and cut the city column from 112 down to the 70px minimum that still keeps 'المدينة' unbroken, letting only the two long city names wrap at their space. Result: zero mid-word splits anywhere, all times on one line, uniform header band, and only 11px of overflow, which falls entirely inside the outer padding of the leftmost cell so no value is hidden. Best reading experience with a negligible, non-scrolling-in-practice cost."},{"name":"one-split-359","widths":[70,56,56,59,56,62],"change":"Keep r0B's in-box discipline but spend the same 289px smarter: move 6px from العشاء to nothing — instead swap the two evening columns so العشاء gets the 62px it needs (41px text, header intact) and المغرب takes the 56px. That removes one of the two header breaks (العشاء no longer orphans 'ء'), keeps every time value whole, and still sums to 359 with no overflow. المغرب, the widest header at 47px, is the single acceptable casualty."}]}
